data.description:
## Description
**What**: Ship plugins/dso/agents/intent-allocation-assistant.md (opus-tier) and wire /dso:preplanning and /dso:implementation-plan to dispatch it only when count(unassigned-or-deferred intent items) > 0. The agent takes the full decomposition tree as structured JSON, unassigned items, and existing manifest entries; it outputs per-item {intent_id, proposed_owner_ticket, proposed_test_artifact, rationale referencing specific ticket attributes, confidence}. Confidence routes acceptance: high pre-accepted, low mandatory review, medium per-item flow; a challenge round forces the planner to identify 1-2 least-confident assignments before proceeding.
**Why**: Reduces manual allocation toil while keeping a human gate on low-confidence and challenge-round items.
**Scope**:
- IN: the agent definition; the threshold-gated dispatch in preplanning and implementation-plan; structured decomposition-tree input; confidence-as-routing; rationale-references-specific-attribute requirement; challenge round.
- OUT: the assistant validation fixture (sc-11).

## Done Definitions

- intent-allocation-assistant.md exists at plugins/dso/agents/ and declares opus tier, accepting the decomposition tree, unassigned items, and existing manifest entries as structured input ← Satisfies: sc-8
- /dso:preplanning and /dso:implementation-plan dispatch the assistant only when the count of unassigned-or-deferred intent items exceeds zero, and skip dispatch when it is zero ← Satisfies: sc-8
- Each assistant suggestion includes proposed_owner_ticket, proposed_test_artifact, a confidence tier, and a rationale that cites a specific ticket attribute rather than a generic owner=current-task assignment ← Satisfies: sc-8
- High-confidence suggestions are pre-accepted with single-item reject available, low-confidence suggestions require explicit review, and medium-confidence suggestions are presented one at a time for accept/edit/reject before the next ← Satisfies: sc-8
- After all suggestions are presented the flow requires the planner to identify 1-2 least-confident assignments as a challenge round before proceeding, and unit tests written and passing cover the threshold-gate and routing logic ← Satisfies: sc-8

## Considerations

- [Adoption] The rationale-must-reference-a-specific-ticket-attribute requirement is the mitigation against the assistant proposing a generic owner=current-task; enforce it in the agent contract.
- [Toil] Confidence-as-routing plus the challenge round bound per-item acknowledge fatigue; medium-tier volume remains a residual risk.

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
data.title: As a planner, I want an opus-tier intent-allocation-assistant agent that proposes owners and test artifacts with confidence-based routing, so unassigned intents get attribute-grounded suggestions.
